A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Composable Interventions for Language Models. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original Llama3-8B experiments composing knowledge editing, compression and unlearning, with results in Figures 2–3 and the main and appendix tables.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments involving other models, overlapping intervention layers, model variants and three-intervention sequences.

M1.justification: The sequential-composition framework and intervention algorithms remain unchanged. The additional model, layer-selection and triplet experiments test the existing framework without introducing a new algorithm or component.

E1.justification: The datasets and domains remain zsRE, WMDP, MMLU and WikiText. Appendix E.4 adds a limited joint-task scenario requiring editing, unlearning and compression within one sequence, whereas v1 evaluates intervention pairs. Additional model configurations are changes to experimental settings.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ten intervention methods: FT, MEMIT, LoRA, Wanda, SparseGPT, AWQ, GPTQ, GA, GD and RMU. Corresponding original comparisons retain their comparator membership; new analyses use selections of these existing methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluations on Mistral 7B Instruct, Yi 1.5 9B Chat, Llama-3 8B Instruct and Llama-3.2 1B. It also introduces overlapping-layer controls and all six orderings of selected intervention triplets on base and instruction-tuned models. These substantially extend the evaluation design; the original Llama3-8B settings remain.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests whether RMU–MEMIT composability depends on modifying separate layers. Appendices E.1–E.2 examine robustness across model families, instruction tuning and size, while E.4 examines performance under three successive interventions. These add substantial analyses beyond v1's pairwise experiments and compression sweeps.

E5.justification: v1 reports editing averages over ten batches without uncertainty estimates. v2's Appendix E.3 and Table 12 add standard errors for editing-compression metrics, discuss MMLU uncertainty, and report approximately 0.5% standard deviation for replicated unlearning experiments. The ten-subset editing count is retained, not explicitly increased; unlearning replication counts and seeds remain unspecified.

E6.justification: Original numerical results in Tables 2–4 and v1 Tables 8–14 are retained, with the latter becoming v2 Tables 15–21. Substantial new results concern layer overlap, additional models and triplets. For example, Table 9 reports MEMIT–Wanda edit-success order sensitivity of .24, .00 and .01 for Llama, Mistral and Yi; Tables 13–14 report triplet edit-success ranges of 93.00–99.50% and 74.82–99.10%.

T1.justification: The intervention definitions, composition notation and Order-free Error and Order Sensitivity equations remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs, and the new experiments introduce no substantive mathematical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the framework, metrics, unified codebase and headline claims about compression, ordering and inadequate general-utility evaluation. Increasing the reported compositions from 310 to 417 and expanding model experiments strengthens the supporting scope without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning transfer across models, instruction tuning and scale, attributes RMU–MEMIT compatibility primarily to algorithmic precision rather than layer separation, and recommends a deployment ordering for triplets. It also adds a WMDP evaluation caveat and reports unsuccessful RMU tuning on Yi. These materially expand mechanisms, applicability boundaries and practical guidance.

D1.justification: The new experiments specify model variants, selected intervention combinations and compression settings, including 25% Wanda sparsity for triplets. Existing Appendix C hyperparameters and code-access information largely remain unchanged. Documentation of the additions is limited: exact overlapping-layer choices and detailed model-specific tuning settings are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Lucki et al. on adversarial unlearning and Jiang et al. and Young et al. for Mistral and Yi. References including Sai et al. on compression and Zou et al. on representation engineering disappear. The overall positioning around independently developed intervention categories remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 tightens several results paragraphs and the conclusion, updates section headings and author information, and changes numerical citations to author–year citations. The main section sequence remains stable. The original extended-results appendix becomes E.5 within an expanded appendix structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 4 and Tables 8–14; Table 12 redisplays existing means with new standard errors, while the other new tables present additional experiments. Table 1 gains a models column. The conference format substantially changes the title and author layout and reflows figures and tables, while retaining the original principal plots.

improvement.justification: Additional model evaluations, a layer-overlap control and uncertainty reporting improve assessability beyond v1's single-model evidence and averages alone. However, new interpretations limit the gain: Appendix D describes increased order sensitivity although Table 8 shows decreases or ties, and E.4.2's recommended triplet ordering is not consistently supported by Tables 13–14. The revision provides useful additional evidence, but its broader practical conclusions require greater care.
